item.title: Comment on Why it is hard for the Executive to disobey the judiciary by Naveen_K
item.description:
The problem in Dilan's reasoning is that just because courts can freeze someone's bank accounts doesn't mean they can force government officials to take specific actions in their job. It's not that simple, at all. Determining what courts can enforce vs. what executive branch officials can legally choose to do is way more complicated than that.

item.title: Comment on The danger of Trump disobeying court orders by PRICES
item.description:
Reply to JFA:

Apparently Tyler edits his comments without telling the readers.

His original comment was "You really think no market prices changed? Also, Weimar economic policy was terrible, so then there was quite a different benchmark."

To get to the substantive question: Tyler, your first question was "If you are especially pessimistic on this front, which are the securities prices that would indicate an actual constitutional problem?"

Depending on what someone thought an "actual constitutional problem" involved, a broad index is not the worst starting place for an analysis. Indeed, isn't your standard refrain to those with whom you are arguing "are you short the market?"

You could look at "connected industries" (which did have positive returns under Mussolini and Hitler), but that doesn't seem to capture what people are talking about when they say constitutional crisis (and that seems to occur with mere changes in policy emphasis and not necessarily indicative of a rise in Fascism). Taking the Bob Higgs understanding of regime uncertainty, one would actually think a broad market index would actually be a good indicator to watch in the event of a switch from a liberal order (as much as Biden's admin was liberal in the classical sense) to a Fascistic regime (as Trump's detractors claim).

Calm down. BE SERIOUS. Stop being hysterical. We should reserve the term FASCIST for when we confront the true thing, lest we degrade it. Besides, history does not simply repeat itself.

We should reserve the term fascist to describe a political movement that gains support by emphasizing negative stereotypes of foreigners and depicts them as a growing threat.

That denigrates the physically disabled and the sexually deviant.

That longs to restore the nation, the true nation, to a golden age before it was betrayed by traitors and degenerates.

That promises to avenge the humiliation it was forced to bear and to redeem its rightful place.

That uses the language of disgust to describe its enemies.

That attacks the press.

That prohibits the use of forbidden words and ideas.

That, with no trace of shame, adopts the big lie.

That incites and excuses and pardons physical violence and intimidation. That has great affection for the tools of violence.

That dreams of aggressive territorial expansion.

That worships the greatness of a strong leader.

That wants to give new powers to the great leader and have his actions go unchecked by the courts or parliament. That refuses restraint. That bypasses the law. That changes the law so he is no more beholden to its nuisance.

Where the opposition is feckless and effete and exhausted and ineffectual.

Where the leader manifests his extreme narcissism with a notably idiosyncratic style of hair and makeup, and is somehow unaware how artificial it looks––how flagrant and monstrous the self-regard.

Where the leader is always perfectly self-assured of his view and his instincts. With never a doubt.

Where there’s the want to put the the leader’s face on the side of a mountain.

Where the center, the wealthy business class, the industrialists fall in line. Where the intellectuals, while find its crudeness distasteful, see the chance to implement experiments that were before now too much for the dotards. Where there’s the chance for a great unfettering, and being rid of programs that subsidize the weak. We’ll focus on practical things, keep things reasonable. The thrill of new ground in a stagnant world.

Where there’s the moment of feeling the shift in what is now permissible. Where the public collectively submits to power. To the sense of an unstoppable force.

Where the church condones hate and violence, and finds the righteous justification in scripture itself.

Where the leader has a great sense of how to precipitate crisis, to create the conditions that permit ever more transgressive acts.

That vigorously salutes with arm raised at a podium on a stage before a great crowd with flags.

That finds an excuse, no matter what. To minimize, and ignore.

Maybe we can only say it’s fascism when we get to the camps. Maybe it’s only when there’s barbed wire and guards with guns. The sweep of the spotlights. When you can see the skull through the skin. Maybe it’s cattle cars and gas chambers and brick crematoria. Maybe only if it’s Zyklon B under the fingernails. Maybe it’s the piles of little leather shoes. Maybe it’s the wheelbarrows. Maybe it’s only when you are walked out to the woods and made to stand on the edge of a pit and shot in the back of the head next to your son.

Maybe its only after the nation goes over the rim, gleefully participating in mass delusion, dragging countless, faceless victims into a chasm of horrific self-destruction.

We are now learning the answer to the greatest question of history in the history of the world. How could a wealthy, civilized country with so many people descend into madness? How could good people let it happen? How could they let it get so far? How could they just go along? Why didn’t they speak up with more force? Why did they not think to act? Could they not see how sick it all was? How they had lost there own sense of what was right and was wrong? Could they not see the rot in their hearts? How they had surrendered to the slow creep of evil? How could they have so willingly let that darkness so deep in their souls?

Now you know.
